from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Can a 1D line fill a 2D square?", 
            "A space-filling curve traverses every point.", 
            "Imagine a vacuum cleaning a room."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Dimensional Paradox", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        point = Dot(color="#00FF00")
        line = Line(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color="#FF00FF")
        square = Square(side_length=2, color="#FFFFFF")
        label_1d = Text("1D", color="#00FFFF", font_size=24)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Can a 1D line fill a 2D square?
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(square))
        self.place_at_grid(line, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.place_at_grid(label_1d, 'C2')
        self.play(Write(label_1d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A space-filling curve traverses every point.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        dot = Dot(color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        # Morph/animate path
        path = VMobject(color="#FFFF00")
        path.set_points_smoothly([self.grid['B2'], self.grid['B5'], self.grid['E5'], self.grid['E2']])
        self.play(Create(path), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Imagine a vacuum cleaning a room.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        vacuum = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(vacuum, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(vacuum))
        self.play(vacuum.animate.move_to(self.grid['E5']), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism: Recursive Construction", 
                          ["We use recursive construction for complexity.", 
                           "Start with a simple generator shape.", 
                           "Iteratively replace segments to fill space."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a square grid (#FFFFFF)
        grid = VGroup()
        for i in range(4):
            for j in range(4):
                cell = Square(side_length=0.7, color=WHITE).shift(self.grid['C3'] + np.array([(j-1.5)*0.7, (i-1.5)*0.7, 0]))
                grid.add(cell)
        self.play(Create(grid))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00") # Highlighting lecture line 1

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight a single cell (#FF0000)
        cell_to_highlight = grid[5]
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(cell_to_highlight, color=RED, buff=0.05)
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate a path winding through the grid (#00FF00)
        path = VMobject(color=GREEN)
        path.set_points_smoothly([grid[i].get_center() for i in [0, 4, 5, 1, 2, 6, 7, 3, 11, 15, 14, 10, 9, 13, 12, 8]])
        self.play(Create(path), run_time=3)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "This maps 1D to 2D space.",
            "As iterations increase, the curve densifies.",
            "A single thread covers the entire plane.",
            "Infinite iterations result in a filled square.",
            "Dimensions collapse into a continuous path."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Mapping (1D to 2D)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create elements
        line = Line(start=LEFT*2, end=RIGHT*2, color="#FFFF00")
        grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.8, stroke_width=1) for _ in range(9)]).arrange_in_grid(3, 3)
        coord_sys = Axes(x_range=[0, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.8)
        path = VMobject(color="#00FF00")
        path.set_points_smoothly([self.grid["A1"], self.grid["B2"], self.grid["C3"], self.grid["C1"], self.grid["A3"]])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(line), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(grid), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(coord_sys), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(Create(path), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Summary", [
            "Curves bridge different dimensional spaces.", 
            "They are infinitely long yet continuous.", 
            "Complexity emerges from simple recursive rules."
        ])
        
        # Visual assets
        # Summarize 1D to 2D
        dim1 = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=BLUE).scale(0.5)
        arrow = Arrow(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        dim2 = Square(side_length=1.0, color=GREEN)
        dim_group = VGroup(dim1, arrow, dim2).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(dim_group, 'B2')
        
        # Key takeaways list (mockup icons)
        takeaway_icons = VGroup(
            Dot(color=YELLOW),
            Dot(color=YELLOW),
            Dot(color=YELLOW)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(takeaway_icons, 'E2')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(dim_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(takeaway_icons[0]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(takeaway_icons[1:]))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(*self.mobjects))

sections.title: Introduction: The Dimensional Paradox
sections.content: Define the goal: Can a 1D line pass through every single point in a 2D square? Introduce the concept of a 'Space-Filling Curve' as a continuous path that visits every coordinate in a finite area.
sections.example: Visualize a robotic vacuum cleaner trying to clean every inch of a square room by moving in a single, non-overlapping line.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Recursive Construction
sections.content: Explain the prerequisite: Understanding 'Iteration' and 'Fractals'. Show how we start with a simple generator shape and replace every line segment with a scaled-down version of itself infinitely.
sections.example: The Hilbert Curve: Start with a 'U' shape, then replace each side with a smaller 'U' pattern, repeating this process to fill the square density.

sections.title: Visualizing the Mapping (1D to 2D)
sections.content: Demonstrate the mathematical mapping. As the curve reaches 'Infinity' in iterations, the line effectively occupies the space, turning a 1D coordinate into a 2D position (x, y) without leaving gaps.
sections.example: An animation showing a single thread unfolding into a 'Peano Curve' that systematically covers a grid, turning a straight line into a dense 'fabric'.

sections.title: Real-World Applications
sections.content: Explain why this matters: Locality. Space-filling curves preserve spatial relationships, making them essential for data indexing and optimization.
sections.example: Database Optimization: Using Z-order curves to store 2D map data in 1D memory, allowing a navigation app to quickly find nearby restaurants by searching only a small segment of the index.

sections.title: Conclusion and Summary
sections.content: Recap: Space-filling curves transform 1D sequences into multidimensional structures. Emphasize that while the line has infinite length, it remains a single continuous path.
sections.example: A final visual of a complex circuit board layout designed using space-filling curves to ensure maximum component density in a tiny device.
